title: The Soul Foundation
summary: These artists helped establish the emotional and musical foundation that modern R&B and hip-hop continue to build upon. Their music emphasizes rich instrumentation, expressive vocals, romance, storytelling, and the connection between gospel, funk, and soul.
educationalConnections: Understanding soul music’s relationship with R&B.
Recognizing the importance of live instrumentation.
Exploring how older recordings become hip-hop samples.
Identifying emotional qualities of vocal performances.
centralLesson: Before hip-hop sampled soul, soul gave hip-hop something to say.

sections.title: Teddy Pendergrass
sections.summary: Teddy Pendergrass matters because the source catalog identifies this route with one of the greatest soul vocalists ever, lead singer of Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes, pioneer of sensual, masculine R&B, king of the “Begging Man” archetype.

sections.title: Ronald Isley
sections.summary: Ronald Isley matters because the source catalog identifies this route with One of the greatest male vocalists in Black music, The embodiment of “Black love song” energy, A vocal chameleon who evolved with every era, The centerpiece of The Isley Brothers for 60+ years.

sections.title: Frankie Beverly & Maze
sections.summary: Frankie Beverly & Maze matters because the source catalog identifies this route with one of the greatest live bands in Black American history, champions of joy, positivity, love, and Black resilience, creators of the most recognizable “vibe signature” in soul music, the soundtrack to barbecues, block parties, family reunions, HBCU homecomings, steady.

sections.title: Chaka Khan
sections.summary: Chaka Khan matters because the source catalog identifies this route with one of the greatest singers in music history, queen of funk & soul, lead vocalist of Rufus before going solo, the blueprint for powerful female voices.
